By the Qinhuai River, teeming with captivating courtesans, Chai Ran’s attention is caught by a certain alluring performer with a lithe figure, long legs, and a mesmerizing dance. Under the guise of indulgence, Chai Ran “supports” this courtesan for two reasons: to enjoy the view and to manipulate hearts. But unexpectedly, he finds himself charmed instead.
This little thing performs a breathtaking dance at the Hundred Flowers Pavilion by night, but by day, works at a pork stall selling meat!
Chai Ran finds himself itching to tear off “her” disguise to see who—or what—is hiding beneath it.

104132.synopsis:
Raven, an S-rank guide, appears before Renault, who lives a modest, inconspicuous life as an A-rank esper.
Raven, who was said to have never exceeded a 10% matching rate with any esper, conspicuously demonstrates a 98.7% matching rate with Renault and becomes his exclusive guide.
While Renault finds Raven disagreeable, he casually goes out to subdue a B-rank monster and ends up facing an unexpected situation, suffering severe injuries.
As Renault stands on the brink of going berserk, Raven lets slip some peculiar words. Only then does Renault realize that Raven was the boy he once saved in the past, and that he is not an ordinary human.
***
“You really don’t remember anything at all?”
Raven muttered, as if amazed. In an instant, the expression vanished from Renault’s pale face.
“What do you mean by that?”
Renault’s voice trembled faintly as he asked. It felt as though the sense of déjà vu and unease that even he could not be certain of had been completely exposed. It felt like he had heard something he shouldn’t have.
“Look at this. I remember everything about you, from start to finish, but you forgot it all. Ah! That’s unfair.”
“What are you talking about right now… that I forgot?”
“I’m starting to feel a little hurt. What should I do?”
It was hard to understand the words of someone who spoke of feeling hurt with a grinning face.
I forgot that brat? That can’t be true. There’s no way I could forget such a striking appearance, nor could I have forgotten those unique, gem-like eyes.
Then why was that brat acting so confidently, as if he knew me? And why was I feeling such an uncomfortable sense of déjà vu?
“Well, it can’t be helped. I’ll just have to kindly go over everything one by one until you remember it all.”
.

A hundred years ago, Chu Xiu from Blue Star transmigrated to the Sky Dome Continent and bound himself to the Heavenly Fate Villain System. He slaughtered holy sons of sacred lands, fathered countless daughters, and fought his way to invincibility among his peers.

In his childhood, Ying Fusheng was loathed by his mother and lived a life without warmth or affection. It wasn’t until he was schemed against and imprisoned that he realized his absurd life of neglect and exploitation was merely a puppet show in a “Swapped Prince” plot.

Meanwhile, Ying Fusheng, the true son of Empress Xu, had been swapped at birth by Consort Ning. He suffered poisoning from his “mother,” found himself imprisoned, and was eventually framed and manipulated by the Fake Prince and the Ning family. He was granted a cup of poisoned wine and executed just as the new Emperor took power…
Opening his eyes once more, he struggled back from the gates of hell to find himself reborn. In this life, he would not follow the same path to ruin.
If his “mother” didn’t fight for favor, then he would be even more “indifferent to fame and fortune.” While others seized power, he planted flowers; while others vied for fame, he chanted sutras.
The Empress Dowager: “Little Six is simple-minded; he’s a filial child.”
Consort Ning: ??
The Crown Prince befriended scholars from humble backgrounds, and the First Prince courted the powerful elite, but Ying Fusheng spent his days with profligate playboys, indulging in “debauchery” and “luxury.”
As the other princes fought tooth and nail, the Emperor looked at Ying Fusheng: “In the end, Little Six is the one who puts my mind at ease the most.”
The Fake Prince: ??
Amidst the tangled roots of the court and the bloodbath of factional struggles, he redressed injustices and settled old debts, one step at a time.
The national treasury flourished, the court rejoiced, and the civil and military officials declared: “His Highness the Sixth Prince is brilliant within and refined without, a man who benefits the entire world!”
The other princes: ??

Later, during a tour of Jiangnan, grievances were redressed and his name echoed across the land…
Beneath Ying Fusheng’s ambition lay a hidden devotion to the common people. Qi Hanzhou is one of those people, and he too is willing to bow down and submit.
Protagonists:
Shou (MC): The ruthless and ambitious True Prince.
Gong (ML): The cold and aloof military official who was once a carefree swordsman in his youth.
Notes:
Alternate history/fictional setting. Semi-serious political intrigue mixed with “dog blood” (melodramatic) face-slapping tropes.
One-sentence summary: The True Prince’s Revenge
Theme: Life’s journey is full of adversity, but we should always face the sun.
